payload.title: FlashAttention-4 and Blackwell Hardware Imbalance
payload.summary: Analysis of how FlashAttention-4 adapts to asymmetric hardware scaling on NVIDIA Blackwell B200, where Tensor Core throughput doubles but shared memory bandwidth and exponential units remain unchanged.

sections.heading: 1. The Problem: Uneven Hardware Evolution
sections.gist: FlashAttention-4 is the first attention implementation deeply optimized for Blackwell B200 GPUs.

sections.heading: 2. Three Core Optimizations
sections.gist: Blackwell's MUFU (Multi-Function Unit) can only perform 16 ops/clock/SM — identical to Hopper.

sections.heading: 3. Critical Analysis: Blackwell-Exclusive Optimizations
sections.gist: The paper is honest: these optimizations are effective only on Blackwell.

sections.heading: 4. CuTe-DSL: What 20-30× Faster Compilation Costs
sections.gist: Another selling point: implementation using Python-embedded CuTe-DSL compiles 20-30× faster than C++ templates.

sections.heading: 5. How Far Can This Approach Go
sections.gist: **Constrained domains will succeed:** Attention, GEMM, sparse matmul — these operators have large but patterned optimization spaces, suitable for extreme optimization.

sections.heading: 6. Transferable Techniques
sections.gist: **Identifying new bottlenecks:** The paper's roofline analysis is solid.

sections.heading: 7. Summary
sections.gist: - **Milestone:** First attention implementation deeply optimized for Blackwell, achieving 71% peak utilization - **Limitations:** Blackwell-exclusive, incompatible with Hopper; B300 hardware changes may invalidate optimizations; baseline c…
